witness.description: Finite set S = {1 <= n < 9699690 : omega(n-j) <= j for all j=1..8}, recomputed from scratch inside the verifier by exact integer trial division; the witness is the expected cardinality and a pure-integer rolling checksum of the sorted element list, both embedded as constants in the verifier (no file I/O).
witness.note: expected_count/expected_checksum are filled by running the verifier's own recompute() once at certificate-generation time; the verifier then fail-closes on any mismatch. Since the verifier recomputes S itself and checks the barrier condition for every element, a PASS is self-witnessing; the constants catch any nondeterminism.

run.detail: TypeError: verify() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given

claim: A PASS (exit 0) establishes the exact finite set S of n < 9699690 satisfying the window-8 barrier omega(n-j) <= j, j=1..8, recomputed and re-checked elementwise by pure-integer trial division — the finite core of R015. It does NOT establish infinitude of B_1: the S->B_1 reduction (Jacobsthal-type periodicity) and all n >= 9699690 remain analytic, outside the trust boundary per lemma L1's own scope.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
